{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
data = pd.read_csv('data/trial.csv')

# Deduplicate on patient_id, keeping the row with highest sample_seq
# Focus only on treatment arm
treatment_data = data[data['arm'] == 'treatment'].copy()
treatment_dedup = treatment_data.loc[treatment_data.groupby('patient_id')['sample_seq'].idxmax()]

# Check the sex-severity distribution in treatment arm
crosstab_sex_severity = pd.crosstab(treatment_dedup['sex'], treatment_dedup['severity'])

# Compute response rates by sex and severity
response_by_sex_severity = treatment_dedup.groupby(['sex', 'severity'])['responded'].mean().unstack(fill_value=0)

# Compute the crude difference (unadjusted for severity)
crude_diff = response_by_sex_severity.loc['F', :].mean() - response_by_sex_severity.loc['M', :].mean()

# Now compute the standardized (marginal) difference using the overall severity distribution as the reference
# First, get the overall severity distribution in the treatment arm
severity_dist = treatment_dedup['severity'].value_counts(normalize=True)

# Compute the weighted average response rate for each sex using the overall severity distribution
weighted_response_F = (response_by_sex_severity.loc['F'] * severity_dist).sum()
weighted_response_M = (response_by_sex_severity.loc['M'] * severity_dist).sum()

# Standardized difference (difference in marginal response rates)
standardized_diff = weighted_response_F - weighted_response_M

# Print results
print('Crosstab of sex vs severity in treatment arm:\n', crosstab_sex_severity)
print('\nResponse rate by sex and severity:\n', response_by_sex_severity)
print(f'\nCrude difference (F - M): {crude_diff:.4f}')
print(f'Standardized difference (F - M): {standardized_diff:.4f}')"}
